necessary_context.content: X is a closed convex subset of R^n. A differentiable prox function d uses the same norm as smoothness; omega(y,x)=d(y)-d(x)-<grad d(x),y-x> >= ||y-x||^2. Definition 2.5 gives monotonicity. Definition 2.6 states the derivative condition and Taylor remainder condition; the latter is ||F(y)-T_{p-1}(y;x)||_* <= L_p||y-x||^p/p!, with T_{p-1}(y;x)=sum_{j=0}^{p-1} D^jF(x)[y-x]^j/j!.
necessary_context.name: Geometry and smoothness

necessary_context.content: A weak epsilon solution satisfies <F(x),xhat-x> <= epsilon for every x in X. Definition 3.1 assumes an Oracle returning a strong VI solution for U_{p,x}(y)=T_{p-1}(y;x)+(2L_p/p!)omega(y,x)^((p-1)/2)(grad d(y)-grad d(x)). Exact solvability is an Oracle capability; this extraction does not establish general efficient implementation or uniqueness.
necessary_context.name: Solution conventions and exact subproblem

necessary_context.content: Theorem 3.3 inherits monotonicity from the problem context, although its displayed statement omits it. Its p=1 case is not covered by the negative powers involving 1/(p-1) used in the printed proof. On p.7 the claimed bound on the sum of squared step quantities does not follow from Lemma 3.2 for an arbitrary comparator without a nonnegativity justification. A uniform stopping budget also needs a finite comparison radius or another justified replacement. These issues are unresolved here.
necessary_context.locator: PDF pp.5–7, Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 3.3 proof
necessary_context.name: Performance proof limitations

necessary_context.content: Section 4 imposes Assumption 4.1, printed as z^(k+1) in z^(0)+sum_{i=1}^k S_F(z^(i)). The lower summation index is 1, as visually checked on PDF p.7. S_F(z)=span{Gamma_{z,F}(a,gamma,m): a in R^p, gamma>0, m>1}, where Gamma is the set of stationary points of the tensor-polynomial family in Eq.(7). The printed sequence is indexed k>=0; at k=0 the displayed sum is empty and would give z^(1)=z^(0), leaving an indexing/boundary ambiguity. No correction to i=0 is established or adopted here. Theorem 4.2 explicitly assumes this model. No unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower bound is extracted.
necessary_context.locator: PDF pp.7–8, Eq.(7), Assumption 4.1 and Theorem 4.2
necessary_context.name: Limits of lower-bound coverage
